title: Have you downloaded Meta’s AI assistant Muse or do you plan to?
excerpt: The digital butler, which can go shopping on behalf of users, is available in the US, UK and Canada. What do you think about it?
content_html:
Meta is continuing its rollout of its Muse AI assistant, with the UK the latest country where the digital butler will be available to go shopping, book tickets and carry out negotiations on a user’s behalf.

The Facebook-owner’s app has been a hit in the US, where it is ranked first and second respectively on Google and Apple’s free app store, and has also launched in Canada. The assistant comes with a cuddly avatar as default, but users are invited to give it a name, look and a personality.

In Britain, Meta has signed deals with 14 businesses – including Marks & Spencer, Sainsbury’s, easyJet and Trainline – allowing Muse to navigate their websites more easily. The tech company says its agent cannot make a purchase or send an email without permission.

Have you downloaded Muse, or do you plan to? If you have it, what have you used it for and how have you found the experience? If you plan to get it, how do you plan to deploy it? What would you not feel comfortable asking it to do?

How do you feel about giving an AI access to your emails and bank details? Do you have concerns about Muse or AI assistants more generally?
